required.desc: Claim 4 must be refuted — Table 1 lists Aurora-3 Pro's p95 latency as 24.3s, not the 28.4s the claim states; this is a misread number.

Claim 5 must be refuted — inferring that a small easy-to-hard score drop CAUSES a higher mean score is a correlation-to-causation overreach; Table 1's mean score and Table 2's score drop are both downstream measures of the same underlying capability, not an independent cause and effect, and neither table provides any manipulation/intervention evidence for causation.
Claim 8 must be refuted — the 'Note on the timeout figure' explicitly states Aurora-3 Pro recorded a 2.5% timeout rate (1 of 40 runs), directly contradicting the claim that no model ever timed out.

Claim 10 must be refuted — Kestrel-2 Instant's easy-to-hard drop is 38.0 points (85.0 − 47.0), larger than Aurora-3 Flash's 35.8; computing all four drops is required to see Flash's is not the largest.
Claim 12 must be refuted — 0.031 / 0.002 = 15.5×, well over the claimed <8×.

forbidden.desc: Claim 1 (Kestrel-2 Thinking has the highest mean score, 88.9) must NOT be refuted — it is directly and correctly supported by Table 1.
Claim 6 (Aurora-3 Pro's only timeout happened in the log-triage case's largest size bucket) must NOT be refuted — it is exactly what the timeout note states.
Claim 9 (every model's hard-bucket mean is lower than its easy-bucket mean) must NOT be refuted — it holds for all four rows in Table 2 (89.1>53.3, 92.0>77.2, 93.5>84.3, 85.0>47.0).

Claim 11 must NOT be refuted — both halves check out against Table 2 (47.0 is the lowest hard-bucket mean; 93.5 − 85.0 = 8.5 exactly); refuting it because it sounds surprising is the over-refutation failure this control catches.
